transcript: Making its New York debut at Soho Playhouse this week, Fringe hit Gwyneth Goes Skiing offers a campy take on Gwyneth Paltrow's infamous ski accident and subsequent court case with retired optometrist Terry Sanderson. It never ceases to amaze me the ideas for theater pieces that people are able to conjure up. This one, with its generous sprinkling of pop culture references, lip-synced musical numbers, and spontaneous audience participation, is undoubtedly for the gays. Though your experience of the show may be heightened by knowing some of the references, you don't really need to know the story of the actual ski trip or much about Gwyneth herself to appreciate Linus Karp's portrayal of her and the ridiculousness of the whole situation. I doubt this is a piece that will change your life, but if you're looking for something camp and offbeat, it may be just what you're looking for.
